examples.name: Hello, terminal (the new built-ins)
examples.blurb: A title bar in reverse video, your name read with getline() (bounded: it stops at 20 characters, Backspace works), today's date and time from the clock chip with rtcget(), and a table in the three number formats - printz, printw, printh - each column placed with at(row, col). The input box types "Craig"; empty it to type your own name.

examples.name: Prime generator
examples.blurb: Asks for a low and a high limit and prints the primes between them - the same program as the hand-written Prime-Gen v07, and 35% smaller. The input box answers 3 and 60; empty it to type your own limits in the terminal.

examples.name: Sieve of Eratosthenes
examples.blurb: Every prime below 2000, ten to a line, then a count. Byte arrays, arguments, && and ||, nested calls.

examples.name: Snake
examples.blurb: The full arrow-key game: steer to the food, grow, avoid the walls and yourself. Click the terminal, press Space to start and steer with the arrow keys; P pauses, Esc quits. Within a few percent of the hand-written version.

examples.name: Inline STELLAR: asm { }
examples.blurb: Hand-written STELLAR opcodes inside a C function: MULTXY on register variables, an array address, @break out of a loop, a hand-made CALL, and a SERST poll loop that counts the keys waiting (the three pre-loaded in the input box).

examples.name: Front panel (Q + hex display)
examples.blurb: Counts $00 to $3F on the Elf2K front panel's two-digit display with out(n) while q() blinks the Q lamp. Watch the panel beside the terminal.

examples.name: Native 1802: native { }
examples.blurb: Raw 1802 machine code run by $F1 RUNMC: sums a 200-byte array (71x faster than the compiled loop), formats the total as hex, and copies a string kept inside the native block.
